newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm despite fears of deep freeze.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm despite fears of deep freeze.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Friday despite fresh fears that some stolen bonds could be frozen and withdrawn from the market, dealers said.

But they said market liquidity was much lower this week amid rumours some banks had been advised that some of their MinFins, totalling more than $50 million in face value, had been frozen after banks reported them stolen.
Still, operators found current prices attractive enough.
But they said recent speculation that frozen MinFins could be confiscated from present holders was a depressing factor and said some Western operators preferred to sit on the sidelines.
Officials from the Finance Ministry and Vneshtorgbank, the main MinFin depositary, have made no official comments on the latest trouble to hit MinFins.
In a similar episode in May, Russian officials froze $24.22 million in Minfins, saying they had been stolen.
"Banks and investors have mixed feelings," one dealer said. "They fear confiscation, but on the other hand, they are finding the risk/return ratio quite interesting."
Dealers said trading was via brokers, with buying seen both inside Russia and abroad.
